items.title: Bill Crow interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: I’d been listening to classical composers that used that kind of harmony anyway, Ravel and Debussy and Mahler.

ctx.x: Wasn’t in the pile, that’s all.

So when I got into the Army, first I came under the influence of this moldy fig who taught me that whole repertoire which has stood me in great good stead as a professional musician, because I know all of the Armstrong stuff, the traditional Chicago jazz tunes. And then another guy came in from Massillon, Ohio, who was a Bebopper. And we said, “What’s Bebop, we don’t know—” And he said, “Well there’s a station out of Chicago late at night we can probably get.” We were stationed in Baltimore at that time. So we…

classical composers that used that kind of harmony anyway, Ravel and Debussy and Mahler. So it just seemed like a natural addition to what I was already listening to but my moldy fig friend was outraged. He said, “You can’t like that music!” I said, “How do I stop myself?” So I didn’t see why I couldn’t play both kinds, and I have to this day.
